guide.title: Your server is ready
guide.lead: Three ways to see something running here in a minute.
guide.hidden: The guide is in your account menu whenever you need it again.
guide.address: Apps get an address like {{example}}, with HTTPS: nothing to set up in DNS.
guide.addressUnknown: The panel could not find this server's IP, so apps get no address yet.
guide.addressPrivate: {{ip}} is a private address: nobody outside the server's own network can reach names made from it, and no certificate can be issued for them. Use the IP people reach the server on.

sample.title: Try a sample app
sample.body: IT Tools, a page of handy converters and generators. One click deploys it at its own address.

templates.title: Install a ready-made app
templates.body: Nextcloud, Ghost, Uptime Kuma, Vaultwarden and more, each with its database when it needs one.

own.title: Deploy your own
own.body: From a Docker image, a Git repository or a Dockerfile.

sample.deploying: Deploying: the image is downloaded once, then it starts. Usually under a minute.
sample.certificate: The first visit can take a few seconds more, while its certificate is issued.
sample.protected: This server is in {{purpose}}, so its sites stay private: opened from the panel, they let you in at once; anyone else is asked for the server's password, user {{user}}. Lost it? Set a new one under Settings, Purpose.
sample.protectedNoUser: This server is in {{purpose}}, so its sites stay private: opened from the panel, they let you in at once; anyone else is asked for the server's password, set under Settings, Purpose.
sample.locked: Choose what this server is for first: until then, every site on it stays locked.
sample.failed: IT Tools could not be deployed.
sample.next: Next: add your own app, or open its page to see its logs, console and domains.

welcome.title: Welcome to Opsifier
welcome.body: A one-minute tour of the panel, in a few stops. Leave it whenever you like with Escape; it stays in your account menu.

guide.title: Start here
guide.body: Deploy a sample app in one click, install one of the ready-made apps, or bring your own. Each gets its own address right away.

project.title: Projects
project.body: A project groups the services that work together: they share a private network and their variables.

domains.title: Every address
domains.body: All the names this panel answers on. New services get one under {{base}} with HTTPS, and you can add your own domains at any time.

activity.title: Work in progress
activity.body: Builds, deploys and backups run here, live. Open one to read its log as it goes.

purpose.title: Who can see the sites
purpose.body: While the server is in development or staging, every site asks for its password and stays out of search engines; opened from the panel, it lets you in without it. In production they are public.

palette.title: Go anywhere
palette.body: Search, or press {{shortcut}}, to open a page or run an action from the keyboard.

account.title: Your account
account.body: Two-factor sign-in, the theme and the language. This tour and the guide are here too, when you need them again.

state.title: A service at a glance
state.body: Its lamp, its replicas and its last deployments, each a mark: problems show before you read a word.

deploy.title: Deploy
deploy.body: Settings you save reach the container at the next deploy. Each one is kept, so you can go back to an earlier version.

open.title: Its address
open.body: Opens the service at its address. Add your own domain under Domains when you are ready.

logs.title: Logs and console
logs.body: Follow its logs live, or open a terminal inside its container.

tabs.title: Everything else
tabs.body: Source, environment, domains, storage, backups and more: one tab for each part.
